text.p: Investors should buy shares of Polish carpet maker Novita SA in the short term and hold them in the long term, the brokerage unit of Bank Handlowy SA said in a report released to the press on Monday.

The report dated October 4 said the company was expected to show an improvement in this year's results and had good long-term prospects but a need to pay off large debt would cap profit margins and dividends this year and in 1997.
On October 4 Novita shares closed at 9.3 zlotys on the Warsaw bourse and closed at 9.4 zlotys on Monday. @
Handlowy expected Novita to raise net profit to 2.6 million zlotys this year and 3.2 million zlotys next year from 1.9 million in 1995.
It said sales would rise to 69.1 million zlotys this year and 85.3 million zlotys next year from 55.1 million in 1995.

Handlowy said Novita had good long-term prospects because of its realised investment programme, developed sales network and diversified production, with the firm producing both floor coverings and various types of industrial fabrics.

But it saw threats in strong foreign competition, an unlikely recovery in housing construction this year and significant indebtedness caused by the investment programme of 22.1 million zlotys in 1994-95 and 3.1 million seen for 1996.
